prompt:
Discuss the validity of the following statements:

Call-by-reference is more powerful than call-by-value.

It is possible to represent infinite lists by using list comprehensions in Erlang.

Closures can be used to provide encapsulation. 15-points

In class-based OO languages, the parameters of overriding methods can be covariant with the corresponding parameters of the overridden methods.

The cost for using virtual functions in C++ is minimal. The response must contain between 256 and 268 words.
judge_reasoning: Candidates [3] and [4] are the only ones that correctly reject statement 4 (covariant parameter types in overriding methods) while also treating statements 1, 3, and 5 as broadly valid. All candidates incorrectly accept statement 2, claiming Erlang list comprehensions can represent infinite lists via laziness, which is not how Erlang list comprehensions work (Erlang is strict/eager). Candidate [1] is wrong on both statement 2 and statement 4 (asserting Scala supports covariant parameters), while candidate [2] is wrong on statement 2 and makes an even stronger incorrect claim that Java/C# allow covariant overriding parameters. [3] slightly better matches the prompt’s wording on statement 5 (“minimal” cost) than [4].
